title: Ops: Unified Fix Actions — convert runbooks into atomic, verifiable admin actions
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Background: Our current runbook corpus is a mix of freeform playbooks, ad-hoc scripts, and operator checklists. This creates brittle manual steps during incidents and makes automation unsafe. Goal: implement a system of 'Atomic Fix Actions' (AFAs) — typed, idempotent, and verifiable operations derived from runbooks. AFAs should be small, composable, and safe to run from the ops console or via automation with clear audit trails and telemetry.

Scope:
- Design an action schema (inputs, outputs, idempotency token, pre-checks, safety-guards).
- Build an authoring flow that converts an existing runbook step into an AFA bundle with a test harness (dry-run, sandbox replay).
- Implement runtime for executing AFAs with built-in retries, circuit-breakers, and canary windows.
- Add observability: traceable action spans, per-action cost/latency, result classification (success, partial, rollback).
- Provide a migration plan for high-risk runbooks (staged conversion + sign-off).

Technical decisions and trade-offs:
- Schema: actions are JSON-LD-like flat objects with versioned schema IDs (to enable backward compatibility). We avoid heavy DSLs to keep authoring simple.
- Execution model: actions run in an 'ops-worker' sandbox with least privilege; side-effects must be declared. This adds surface area but enforces safety.
- Idempotency: every action requires an idempotency key derived from (action_id, target, intent_uuid). For long-running steps we store progress checkpoints to allow safe retries.
- Rollbacks: not all actions will be auto-rollbackable. For those that are not, the action must include a reversible companion (or a two-phase commit style pattern).
- Language/runtime: initial AFAs implemented as TypeScript microhandlers (fast iteration + existing infra). We will standardize an HTTP/gRPC contract so other languages can be supported later.

Implementation plan (high level):
1) Design schema + small reference implementation AND test harness. (Week 1)
2) Build authoring UI modal in Console for creating and previewing an AFA from a runbook step; wire to Dry-run cluster. (Week 2)
3) Implement ops-worker runtime with sandboxing, telemetry injection, and idempotency store. (Week 3)
4) Migrate 5 low-risk runbooks to AFAs and run shadow executions for 48h. (Week 4)
5) Release opt-in canary in Console and runbook library; collect metrics and iterate.

Acceptance criteria:
- AFA schema v1 defined and documented in a Design doc link below.
- Authoring modal exists and can convert a runbook step into an AFA bundle and submit a dry-run.
- ops-worker can execute AFAs with idempotency guarantees and emits traces that join to request/investigation traces.
- 5 production runbooks migrated, run successfully in shadow mode for 48h, and one end-to-end canary completed with no customer-visible incidents.
- Rollout dashboard shows per-action success rate, median latency, and number of rollbacks.

Safety & security:
- All AFAs must include a has_sensitive_targets boolean and require elevated approval flow when true.
- Ensure KMS usage for any secrets; workers never receive raw credentials.
- Security review required before merging any action that touches billing, customer data, or IAM.

Testing plan:
- Unit tests for action handlers and idempotency logic.
- Integration tests against a sandboxed cluster with synthetic artifacts.
- Canary: shadow-run converted runbooks for 48h, then a gradual opt-in rollout to SREs, then broader ops team.

Monitoring & SLOs:
- Action success rate target >= 99% for non-invasive actions.
- Latency P95 < 2s for quick checks; long-running actions report progress and timeouts.

Notes and links:
- Design doc: https://docs.redwood.company/concord-actions/design-v1
- UX mockups (Drive): https://drive.google.com/drive/fake-link/concord-actions-mockups
acceptance_criteria: 1) Schema v1 published and recorded in the design doc link. 2) Authoring modal in Console can create and submit an AFA dry-run. 3) ops-worker executes with idempotency; traces appear in Jaeger and link to investigation IDs. 4) 5 low-risk runbooks migrated and shadowed for 48h. 5) Rollout dashboard reports metrics and shows no regressions for 72h after canary.
